handoff.purpose: Implements _emit, builds three layers (imports, symbols, documents), assembles header and returns GraphBrief; also provides render_brief convenience wrapper.

symbols.name: _emit
symbols.note: Closure capturing spent, budget_chars, counts, dropped, rendered. Renders a layer if it fits within budget.

symbols.name: graph_brief
symbols.note: Builds GraphBrief from index; uses _emit for layers. Returns GraphBrief namedtuple.

symbols.name: render_brief
symbols.note: Convenience wrapper returning graph_brief(...).text or '' on failure.

claims.text: The header is written last but must not escape the budget, so its space is reserved up front.
claims.why: spent is initialized to _HEADER_RESERVE before any _emit calls, reserving space for header.

claims.text: Small high-value layers are rendered first and DISPLAYED in reading order.
claims.why: _emit is called in order imports, symbols, documents; display order is symbols, imports, documents (line 387).

claims.text: Artefact importers are filtered HERE as well as in the neighbourhood.
claims.why: Both edges.get(rel) and reverse.get(rel) are filtered through _is_artefact.

claims.text: PUBLIC API ONLY for a neighbour. What a caller may use from another module is its public surface; its private helpers are not callable and listing them cost 495 lines around ``offload.py`` -- enough to consume the whole budget on names nobody is allowed to reference.
claims.why: file_symbols(path, include_private=False) is called for neighbours.

claims.text: Both keys are absent unless the document layer is enabled, so this section vanishes rather than lying when it is off.
claims.why: The document layer is only built if include_docs is True; rev and wiki are obtained via .get() which returns {} if key missing.

claims.text: DISPLAY order, independent of the priority order the layers were rendered in: symbols first because 'what exists' is what a writer needs before anything else, then who reaches whom, then what has been promised.
claims.why: sections is built as [rendered[k] for k in ('symbols','imports','documents') if k in rendered].

claims.text: It must never raise into a lane, so a failure to describe the graph degrades to no description.
claims.why: render_brief wraps graph_brief in try/except and returns '' on any exception.
